intro: To add a chart in Pages on Mac, open your document, click Insert Chart in the toolbar, and choose a style from 2D Charts, 3D Charts, or Interactive. Then select the chart, click Edit Chart Data, type your numbers into the Chart Data editor, and close the editor to see the result.
tldr: Click Insert Chart in the Pages toolbar, then choose 2D Charts, 3D Charts, or Interactive.
Select the chart, click Edit Chart Data, and type your labels and numbers in the editor.
Use the top-right button in the Chart Data editor to switch rows and columns.
Close the editor to see the chart. Shift-Command-D (⇧⌘D) shows or hides the editor.
These steps follow Apple's guide for Pages 15.4, which needs macOS 26 or later.

blocks.text: Pages puts charts behind one toolbar button. Apple's guide for Pages on Mac names that button and does not describe a menu item for charts, so these steps stick to it. They follow Apple's guide for Pages 15.4, which requires macOS 26 or later.
What you need before you add a chart

Open Pages and check your version first. Choose Pages > About Pages from the menu bar. If the version is lower than 15.4, update before you follow these steps, because the toolbar in older releases may not match. You also need a document open. A new blank one works fine.

Cost is the other question. Apple says creating, viewing, editing, and real-time collaboration in Pages do not need a subscription. Apple Creator Studio is a separate paid option that adds premium content and intelligent features. Adding a chart is editing, so these steps need no subscription.
Choose 2D, 3D, or Interactive for your data

After you click Insert Chart, you pick a family: 2D Charts, 3D Charts, or Interactive. Each family has several styles, and you scroll left or right in the list to see more. Scroll through the whole list before you choose, since the first styles you see are not the only options.

Apple's guide does not say which family suits which data, so judge by the style itself. A 3D chart can make values harder to compare, because depth can make a bar look bigger or smaller than it is. For a report or a printout, a flat 2D style is usually the safer choice.
Enter your numbers in the Chart Data editor

Select the chart by clicking it, then click the Edit Chart Data button near it. The Chart Data editor opens. Type your labels and numbers into its table. When you finish, close the editor to return to the chart and check the result.

The keyboard helps here. Shift-Command-D (⇧⌘D) shows or hides the Chart Data editor, so you can reopen your data without going back to the toolbar. Apple also says some shortcuts can be changed in System Settings, so your combination may differ from the list.
Switch rows and columns when the chart looks wrong

Sometimes the chart draws lines or bars that do not match your table. The usual cause is the series setting. A series is one group of values, such as one product, and the chart gives each series its own color or line. The Chart Data editor has a button in its top-right corner that switches whether rows or columns form the series.

Here is a worked example. Say your table has months down the first column and three products across the top. With products as the series, each product gets its own color, and the months run along the axis. Flip the series, and each month gets its own color while the products run along the axis. Neither view is wrong, so pick the one that answers your question.
Why a large table can show only part of your data

Column, bar, line, and area charts can show a sample when your table is large. The data table itself stays complete. The chart draws a representative sample of each series instead. A message appears under Large Data Set in the Chart tab of the Format sidebar when this happens.

Apple's fix is to build the chart from a smaller table or a smaller selection. Select only the rows you need, then create the chart from that. The chart then shows the specific points you chose. If a line chart seems to leave points out, check the Format sidebar before you change your data.
Delete a chart without losing the table behind it

To delete a chart, click it and press Delete. Deleting the table data that feeds a chart does not remove the chart. It only clears the chart's data. If you delete the rows and see a blank chart, the chart is still on the page, so click it and press Delete.

blocks.caption: Differences between Apple's Mac and iCloud chart guides.

blocks.text: Pages for iCloud works in a browser and uses the same Chart button in the toolbar. It offers 2D or Interactive styles when you insert a chart. It starts the editor with placeholder data, and you close that editor with the X in the top-left corner.

Be careful with 3D charts moving between apps. If you import a document with a 3D chart into Pages for iCloud, the chart shows as 2D. Apple says the 3D information is saved. Open the file in the Pages app on a Mac, iPhone, or iPad, and the chart shows in 3D again.
Why the Edit Chart Data button might be missing

Apple's documentation does not describe a fix for a missing Edit Chart Data button. The checks below are the sensible next steps, but they are not guaranteed repairs. Try them in order and stop when the button appears.

items: Click the chart once to select it. Apple's steps place the Edit Chart Data button near the chart, after you select it.
Confirm your version. Pages 15.4 requires macOS 26 or later, so an older Mac may not match these steps.
Check that you are in the Mac app. Pages for iCloud uses a different editor, with placeholder data.
Contact Apple Support if the button still does not appear. The Pages guide does not cover this case.

blocks.text: Common mistakes when adding a chart in Pages

items: Looking for an Insert menu item. Apple's chart steps refer only to the Insert Chart toolbar button.
Expecting an insert shortcut. The only chart shortcut Apple lists is Shift-Command-D, and it shows or hides the editor.
Picking a 3D style for a report. Flat 2D bars and lines are easier to compare.
Deleting table rows and assuming the chart is gone. The chart stays on the page with no data.
Using a large table and expecting every row to appear. Large series show a sample instead.
Editing data and never closing the Chart Data editor. Close it to return to the chart and check the result.

blocks.text: Keyboard shortcuts and what Apple does not document

Apple's keyboard shortcuts page for Pages lists one chart shortcut, Shift-Command-D (⇧⌘D). It shows or hides the Chart Data editor. The page does not list a shortcut that inserts a chart. It also says some shortcuts can be changed in System Settings and may not match the list. To see what is set on your Mac, open System Settings > Keyboard > Keyboard Shortcuts and check the entries for Pages.
Versions, pricing, and what to read next

The version you run decides which guide you follow. MacRumors reported that the older Mac Pages app moved to version 14.5 and will receive no new features. The newer Creator Studio edition is version 15.1, and the steps in this guide come from the 15.4 guide, which is part of that newer line.

Once the chart is in place, you may want to [save the document as a Word file](/how-to/save-as-a-word-file-in-pages) before you share it. If the document runs to many pages, [add page numbers in Pages on Mac](/how-to/add-page-numbers-in-pages) next. Changes from other people are easier to review with [Track Changes in Pages on Mac](/how-to/turn-on-track-changes-in-pages).

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to insert a chart in Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: Apple's keyboard shortcuts page does not list one for inserting a chart. The only chart shortcut it lists is Shift-Command-D (⇧⌘D), which shows or hides the Chart Data editor. Apple also says some shortcuts can be changed in System Settings.

faq.question: Where is the Insert Chart button in Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: It sits in the toolbar along the top of the Pages window. Apple's chart guide refers to it by that name and does not describe a menu item for inserting charts. If your window looks different, check the version in Pages > About Pages.

faq.question: Which version of Pages do these steps need?
faq.answer: These steps follow Apple's guide for Pages 15.4, which requires macOS 26 or later. Apple's What's new page says so. Older Pages releases may not match the toolbar and menus described here.

faq.question: Do I need to pay to add a chart in Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Apple's newsroom says Keynote, Pages, Numbers, and Freeform stay free to create and edit for all users. Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year in the U.S. and adds premium content and intelligent features.

faq.question: Can I add a chart in Pages for iCloud?
faq.answer: Yes. Click the Chart button in the toolbar, then choose 2D or Interactive. Pages for iCloud opens the Chart Data Editor with placeholder data, and you close it with the X in the top-left corner.

faq.question: Why does my chart show only part of my data?
faq.answer: Column, bar, line, and area charts can show a representative sample when the table is large. Apple's fix is to build the chart from a smaller table or selection. The Format sidebar shows a Large Data Set message when this happens.

faq.question: How do I delete a chart in Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: Click the chart and press Delete. Deleting the table data behind a chart does not remove the chart. It only clears the chart's data, so use Delete on the chart itself.

faq.question: Can I switch rows and columns after I add the chart?
faq.answer: Yes. Open the Chart Data editor, then use the button in its top-right corner to switch whether rows or columns form the series. Apple's guide describes this as the way to change series.

steps.name: Open the document
steps.text: Open the document in Pages and scroll to the page where the chart belongs. A chart needs its own space, so leave room for it on that page.

steps.name: Click Insert Chart in the toolbar
steps.text: Look along the top of the Pages window for the toolbar. Click the Insert Chart button. Apple's chart steps refer only to this button.
steps.tip: Apple's chart guide does not mention an Insert menu item for charts, so you do not need to search the menu bar.

steps.name: Choose 2D Charts, 3D Charts, or Interactive
steps.text: After you click Insert Chart, choose a family: 2D Charts, 3D Charts, or Interactive. Scroll left or right to see more styles in that family. Look at each style before you decide.

steps.name: Click a style or drag it onto the page
steps.text: Click the style you want, or drag it onto the page where it belongs. Apple's guide lists both methods as ways to add the chart.

steps.name: Select the chart and click Edit Chart Data
steps.text: Click the chart to select it. Then click the Edit Chart Data button near the chart. The Chart Data editor opens, and this is where your numbers go.

steps.name: Enter your labels and numbers
steps.text: Type your category labels and values into the Chart Data editor. The chart is built from whatever this table holds, so a typo here shows up in the chart. Check each value before you close the editor.
steps.tip: A long table can show a sample in the chart rather than every point. The troubleshooting section explains the fix.

steps.name: Switch rows and columns if the chart looks wrong
steps.text: Look at the top-right corner of the Chart Data editor. Click the button there to switch whether rows or columns form the data series. Use it again to undo the change.

steps.name: Close the editor and check the chart
steps.text: Close the Chart Data editor to return to the chart. Check the labels, the values, and the series. To reopen the editor later, press Shift-Command-D (⇧⌘D).

steps.name: Adjust the chart in the Format sidebar
steps.text: Open the Format sidebar and use the Chart tab to adjust how the chart looks. If your table is too big to draw in full, the Large Data Set message appears here.
steps.tip: Check this tab first when a chart seems to leave points out.

shortcuts.action: Show or hide the Chart Data editor

troubleshooting.problem: Edit Chart Data button is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Click the chart once to select it, then look near it for the button. Confirm you have Pages 15.4 on macOS 26 or later. Apple's guide documents no fix beyond these checks, so contact Apple Support if the button still does not appear.

troubleshooting.problem: Chart shows only part of my data
troubleshooting.fix: Your table is probably large, so the chart draws a sample. Check the Large Data Set message in the Chart tab of the Format sidebar. Build the chart from a smaller table or a smaller selection of rows.

troubleshooting.problem: Chart is still there after I deleted its data
troubleshooting.fix: That is expected. Deleting table data clears the chart but does not remove it. Click the chart and press Delete to remove it from the page.

troubleshooting.problem: 3D chart shows as 2D in Pages for iCloud
troubleshooting.fix: Pages for iCloud shows 3D charts from an imported document as 2D. Apple says the 3D information is saved. Open the file in the Pages app on your Mac, iPhone, or iPad to see it in 3D again.

troubleshooting.problem: Chart style list does not show every style
troubleshooting.fix: Scroll left or right in the list of chart styles. Apple's guide says more styles appear when you scroll that way.

troubleshooting.problem: Chart shows rows and columns swapped
troubleshooting.fix: Use the button in the top-right corner of the Chart Data editor to switch rows and columns, then check the chart again.
